Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Redwood] Immediate guidance: routing advisory for multi-zone disruption

Hi Samantha / Acme ops team,

We’re seeing degraded connectivity affecting our EU and APAC hosted inference clusters due to an upstream networking anomaly at a major cloud provider. Impact is limited to traffic that is pinned to the affected zones; US regions remain healthy.

Short-term actions you can take immediately to reduce latency errors and keep requests flowing:
- If your integration points to a region-specific endpoint (for example, region=eu-west or host eu1.redwood.ai), switch to the global endpoint (api.redwood.ai) to allow automatic smart routing.
- Alternatively, add the X-Redwood-Region header set to "us-west" (header name: X-Redwood-Region: us-west) for immediate routing to unaffected capacity.
- Reduce request concurrency briefly (10–20%) to avoid cold-start pressure while caches warm at the alternate region.

We’ve attached a short playbook with the exact curl examples and a small script your SREs can drop into CI/CD. I’ll copy the internal ops team and Jonas for any account-specific assistance.

We expect continued intermittent impact to EU/APAC over the next 6–12 hours while the provider completes route stabilization; we’ll follow up with a full timeline and post-incident summary.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep this thread updated. If you want immediate help doing the switch, reply and we’ll hop on a screenshare.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Multi-zone disruption — preliminary RCA & mitigation steps

Team — internal summary and next steps (for postmortem):

What happened (preliminary):
- 2028-03-21 07:58 UTC: Major provider announced route flap affecting eu-west-1 and apac-southeast-1 edge routers.
- Result: A subset of our inference nodes in those zones experienced packet loss and elevated latency; smart routing did not reassign all pinned sessions quickly enough because of a TTL problem in our edge cache invalidation logic.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Forced cache invalidation for pinned region headers across our front doors (applied 08:06 UTC).
- Expanded temporary capacity in us-west to accept rerouted traffic.
- Enabled a short-lived fallback policy that allows requests with region=eu to be processed in us-west.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Rishi: change cache TTL behavior to reduce window for pinned sessions (P1, ETA 48h).
- Lauren: confirm autoscale thresholds and adjust to prevent queueing during mass reroutes (P1, ETA 24h).
- Marissa: track customer SLA claims and coordinate credits (P2, ongoing).

Notes: we’re drafting the full postmortem doc and publishing it to the Drive link in this thread. Attachments include the raw timeline CSV and a set of traces for three impacted customers (redacted).

—Jonas

- Action plan: we will implement the TTL and autoscale changes Jonas listed within 72 hours; Rishi and Lauren will confirm and share a timeline.
- SLA/credits: Marissa will follow up with a formal credit determination and a small operational credit to cover the window where your requests saw increased errors.

If you’d like a short 30-minute review call this week to walk the timeline and the fixes, let me know availability and we’ll schedule. We appreciate the trust and are sorry for the disruption.
